newsitem.title: GERMANY: German FinMin says has no plans to sell gold.
newsitem.headline: German FinMin says has no plans to sell gold.

text.p: Germany has no plans to sell gold to aid the federal budget, a Finance Ministry spokeswoman said on Thursday.
She was commenting on a report in the Handelsblatt newspaper that some members of the coalition want the government to sell Bundesbank gold reserves to avert tax increases.
The spokeswoman said the government has no plans to make such a recommendation to the Bundesbank.
Coalition sources confirmed, however, that plans have been drawn up in this direction. Chancellor Helmut Kohl's coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) are particularly opposed to tax increases.
Handelsblatt said the Bundesbank holds 95 million ounces in gold reserves that were originally acquired at an average price of 144 marks an ounce, for a total value of 13.7 billion marks.

At the current market value of about 600 marks an ounce, it would be worth about 57 billion marks, it said, adding that some coalition members were contemplating a change in the Bundesbank law to make use of these hidden reserves of over 40 billion marks.
Experts from federal, state and local governments, concluding a three-day meeting today, are expected to announce that tax revenues are 20 billion marks below budgeted levels.
